title: CupOFMoCA: Coupled Objective-Guided Discrete Flows for Molecular Conjugate Assembly
claim: Guiding a pre-trained discrete flow with objective scores and hard validity masks turns unassembled components into valid coupled assemblies.
layout: 2 panels stacked; A left-to-right branching flow, B timeline with update formula
description: Panel A is a left-to-right flow. On the left, a grey cloud labeled 'Prior μ0 / Unassembled' holds loose peptides, stars (drugs) and warhead/ligand shapes. A horizontal line labeled 'Discrete Flow Φθ^{0→T}' runs right, with text for property predictors and validity constraints beneath it. It splits into two arrows. The top arrow goes to a brown 'Assembled PDC' bubble and the bottom arrow to a blue 'Assembled PROTAC' bubble. Each bubble shows assembled molecules and has a column of checkbox labels such as attachment compatibility, linker feasibility and representational validity. Panel B is a timeline from t=0 to t=1. A highlighted segment between t=k and t=k+1 sits under a formula for the tilted, masked distribution p'(Z') ∝ p_{k+1}(Z') exp(βS(Z')) 1_valid(Z'). Small boxes below give the sampling and acceptance rules. A cupcake mascot sits in the bottom-right corner.
caption: Overview of CupOFMoCA for molecular conjugate generation. (A) A pre-trained discrete flow model is guided from unassembled components to valid assembled conjugates, including peptide-drug conjugates (PDCs) and PROTACs, under objective guidance and hard validity constraints (attachment compatibility, linker feasibility, and representational validity). (B) Objective-guided sampling with hard validity constraints. We reweight candidate probabilities with objective scores and exclude invalid updates with a validity mask. The illustrated PDC acceptance rule retains updates that preserve or increase the score. For PROTACs, we accept valid tilted proposals and return the highest-scoring valid state encountered.
abstract: Molecular conjugates, including PROTACs and peptide-drug conjugates (PDCs), derive their function from the joint behavior of multiple coupled components, yet most generative approaches design these components independently and combine them only after generation. Such staged pipelines ignore cross-component dependencies and often produce conjugates that are chemically invalid, fall outside empirical conjugate distributions, or lose function upon assembly. In this work, we introduce Coupled Objective-Guided Discrete Flows for Molecular Conjugate Assembly (CupOFMoCA), a discrete generative method that enforces cross-component chemical constraints during conjugate generation. CupOFMoCA restricts guided updates to chemically feasible conjugate states and reweights local transitions using molecular design objectives. Across three PDC systems, coupled generation achieved 100% conjugation validity among valid peptides and increased valid yield over matched post-hoc filtering, with comparable predicted binding scores across the full valid sets. In three-seed evaluations of three PROTAC systems, CupOFMoCA achieved the highest assembly validity on two systems and generated more assembly-valid molecules per second than the evaluated baselines. We further evaluated the generated PROTACs with post-hoc DegradeMaster scoring and explicit-solvent molecular dynamics, supporting their predicted activity and conformational properties. Together, these results establish CupOFMoCA as an efficient generator of molecular conjugates, supporting therapeutic development via coordinated control of assembly and molecular properties.
